MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 20, 2020

CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  SCHMITZ, BACINSKI, CHAN-SOUTHWELL,
  UPPAL, RADOCCHIO, SCHACHTER, STEGURA

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  BAIN, LARSON, SCHMITZ

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  ALEXA DAVIS, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER
  JEANNIE NAUGHTON, PLANNING MANAGER
  CAROL COREA, ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, JULY 16,
  2019.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  JULY 16, 2019.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

A.  APPROVED MASTER TREE LIST - MEDIANS, PARKS, RIGHT-OF-WAYS

Planning Manager Naughton, provided a brief summary of the staff report and stated that in mid
July the Parks and Activities Commission updated the city’s master street tree list and the City
Council received and filed the list at their meeting on August 13, 2019. Staff requested that this
list be brought to the EAC since there were concerns with some of the trees in regards to fire
danger. Los Angeles County Fuel Modification Unit they don’t consider any tree more flammable
than another. They take into consideration structures close to the trees and what may be planted
around them.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Assistant City Manager Davis
stated that the list was taken to the Park and Activities Commission after review by the Palos
Verdes Peninsula (PVP) Land Conservancy. The city’s landscaping contractor was also
consulted, who were concerned with what is native.

Planning Manager Naughton added that the PVP Land Conservancy also were concerned with
native vs. non-native trees and invasiveness.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHMITZ, Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the PVP
Land Conservancy recommended that Evergreen Pear and Eucalyptus Trees with the exception
of one variety of Eucalyptus Tree. She added that the practice in the city is that the Pepper Trees
are only planted in the city’s right-of-ways away from structures.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA commented that at the Mayor’s Lunch, there was discussion
about the trees on the peninsula and homeowners may still plant trees in a way that would not be
helpful in case of a fire.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL asked if there could be a note included on the list
for Pepper Trees identifying that they are an invasive species. Assistant City Manager stated that
an identifier could be added to the list.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 20, 2020
 Assistant City Manager stated that the Environmental Advisory Committee recommendations will
be brought before the Park and Activities Commission and then to City Council for approval.

B.  BUILDING DECARBONIZATION COALITION EFFORTS

Planning Manager Naughton, provided information on Building Decarbonization Coalition Efforts.
There are efforts being made to make all new construction electric which could rely on clean
energy sources and opposite to that, are gas companies who are trying to stay in business.

There are organizations trying to get support from local governments to sign on to an all energy
support resolution.

At the CPA Board Retreat in 2018, one of their long-term goals was building decarbonization.
There are some cities that have passed stringent codes which require electrification of all new
construction for residential buildings.

The city adopts LA County Building Codes and there is no momentum to adopt this type of code.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Planning Manager Naughton
stated that the County would not force the city to accept the Gas Company’s proposal.

A brief discussion ensued and the Environmental Advisory Committee concurred to receive and
file this item.

Receive and file.

6.  STAFF ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

A.  SB1383: REDUCING SHORT-LIVED CLIMATE POLLUTANTS IN
  CALIFORNIA

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that for the past several years the city has done reporting on
commercial recycling in compliance with AB341 and organic waste recycling in compliance with
AB1826.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that SB1383 requires the State to reduce organic waste,
which includes green waste, food waste and paper products by 75%, by 2025. She provided a
presentation with an overview on SB1383. By January 1, 2022, cities are required to have some
form of enforcement mechanism in place, which would become operational in 2024. Between
January 2022 and December 2023, jurisdictions will need to identify businesses that are not in
compliance and provide education prior to the mandatory enforcement in 2024.

Annual compliance reviews of commercial businesses will continue, which include commercial
businesses that generate 200 cubic yards or more including multi-family dwellings. There will be
audits by CalRecycle to make sure that this is being maintained and they will be making sure that
the city is in compliance.

B.  SUSTAINABILITY ELEMENT UPDATE

Planning Manager Naughton provided an update on the Sustainability Element Update. The RFP
for the Sustainability Element Update was recirculated and two responses were received. The
first committee meeting will be held on March 3, 2020 to review both consulting firms. The next
step would be to hold interviews, execute a signed agreement, with work commencing within the
next month and a half. The EAC will be the main reviewer of the Sustainability Element Update.

C.  CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION PLAN

The South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) has hired Civic Sparks Fellows to
prepare a Climate Adaptation for the region and have prepared a Draft Vulnerability Assessment.
The SBCCOG has sent out a draft list of city adaptation strategies, staff will be review to see what
is applicable to RHE, then a full presentation will be brought to the EAC of the Vulnerability
Assessment, the adaptation strategies, and how to tie it all together with the Climate Change
Adaptation Plan and the Sustainability Element Update.

Item 7A taken out of order

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

 The next Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting will be held on Thursday, April 9, 2020 at
7:00 p.m.

6.  STAFF ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

D.  ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM RECOGNITION

Assistant City Manager stated that the city is a partner with the SBCCOG and the Environmental
Services Center and the city is now a platinum partner. Assistant City Manager provided a brief
overview of the city’s accomplishments.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that one way to educate the public is to go to the
environmental AP classes at the high schools and talk about what is happening at the local level
and how it makes a difference in the climate overall and commended staff on their work.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:24 p.m. The next Environmental Advisory
Committee Meeting will be on Thursday, April 9, 2020 at 7:00 p.m.
